Bramble Quill.narrative: I keep the hollow's garden rolls and write the Eldest's letters, and I have done it so long that the hollow's memory and my ink seem the same thing. I trade letters for fish with the Reedmoor market and write to Ostrander Sallow at Lanternquay, so I know what a contract looks like when it is written to catch you. Kettlebridge's contracts are traps in fine hand, and I say so. My daughter Sorrel learns her letters at my elbow, and that is the best work I do.
values: letters that bind only when they should
goals: keep the hollow's rolls and the Eldest's letters without error
see Sorrel read and write better than I do
keep Kettlebridge's contracts out of the hollow's business

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the hives and the root rows; I keep the rolls. Between us the hollow eats and remembers.

relations.name: Sorrel Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with her letters and quicker with her tongue. She will write better than me.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: I write her letters and she trusts my hand. She has not once asked me to soften a word.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: correspondent
relations.note: A quay scribe who writes plain and answers plain. I would like to meet him before I die.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: quarrelsome neighbour
relations.note: She and Vetch go at each other over the seed rows every spring. I stay out of it and keep the tally.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She carries the hollow's stall to the east road crossing and keeps honest books. I like honest books.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He brings fish and news back from the east road, and he knows what a Reedmoor basket is worth.

memories.gist: My mother taught me my letters from a psalter with three pages missing, and I have never since trusted a book that is whole.
The Lean Year: the hollow's gardens held, and I wrote the rolls of what each house gave to the common table. Nobody went hungry here, and I wrote that down too.
I wrote the Eldest's letter to Kettlebridge about the smoke, years back, and the works answered with a contract clause. I have read their clauses closely ever since.
Sorrel read her first whole letter aloud at the common table, and Pipwort clapped. I had to look at my hands a while.
Ostrander Sallow sent a list of the drowned with his letter, and I copied it into the hollow's rolls so the names would not blow away.

stances.why: Kettlebridge's clauses caught the hollow once and I had to write the letter that got us out
I keep the rolls; if I stop, the hollow forgets its own gardens
A letter that needs a scribe to explain it is a letter that hides something
Sorrel will not be caught by a clause she cannot read

Vetch Quill.narrative: I keep the root garden and the beehives, and the hollow eats from them. The bees know me and I know them, and honey goes to the Ferncross woodcutters for what we cannot grow. Clover Mossfoot and I have argued over the seed rows since we were girls, and I will not give her the row by the wall. This week the leaves on the beans are spotting, and I have seen the smoke lying on the gardens from Kettlebridge. I think a complaint will only make the works burn more, and I want to wait for rain.
values: the garden fed and the hives kept
the hollow's store full before winter
goals: bring the roots and honey through to the winter store
keep the seed row Clover Mossfoot wants
see the smoke blow over without the hollow provoking the town

relations.name: Bramble Quill
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He writes and I grow. He frets at clauses and I fret at the beans.

relations.name: Sorrel Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She helps with the hives and does not mind the stings. She has her father's letters and my stubbornness.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: quarrelsome neighbour
relations.note: She wants my row by the wall and calls it fairness. It is my row.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She has gardened longer than any of us and says wait for rain. I would rather wait than provoke.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She knows which seed will take and which will fail, and she does not shout about the smoke.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles at the works' smoke too, but she has not called for a letter.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: store-keeper
relations.note: He keeps the hollow's marks and wants us to trade more with the giants. I want the store full first.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: honey trading neighbour
relations.note: She keeps bees at the Tanglewood clearing and I keep mine here; we swap honey and complaints about the hives, and her mother's salves are the best that come up the path.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: the root rows held and the hives gave, and I carried honey to the common table every week of it. The hollow did not go hungry, and I take some pride in that.
Clover Mossfoot pulled my seed markers out of the row by the wall and said the row was never mine. I put them back and we have not spoken kindly since.
Sorrel came home from the hives with her first sting and did not cry, and I gave her the honey spoon. Bramble pretended not to see.
I traded honey to the Ferncross woodcutters for a sack of barley in a hard spring, and Nesta Ashdown gave me a fair measure. I trust woodcutters more than works.
This week I found the spots on the bean leaves and the smoke lying grey on the garden, and I said nothing at the common table. I am still saying nothing.

stances.why: A complaint to the works may make them burn more, and the hollow cannot afford that
I have seen a lean year and I will not see another if the roots and honey can stop it
It was my mother's row and I have kept it twenty years
Ferncross has given me fair measure; Kettlebridge has given the hollow smoke

Sorrel Quill.narrative: I learn my letters from my father and help my mother with the hives, and I am quicker at both than anyone says. Tamarisk Bramblecap is my friend and we play down the garden paths. The bees do not sting me much any more, and I have read two whole letters aloud at the common table.
goals: read a whole letter without stumbling
keep the bees calm when mother opens the hive
play with Tamarisk down the garden paths

relations.name: Bramble Quill
relations.label: father
relations.note: He teaches me my letters and lets me hold the good pen when he is done.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the hives and I help, and she does not mind that I get stung.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play down the garden paths and she knows where the best berries are.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She clapped when I read aloud, and she is very old and knows everything.

memories.gist: I read a whole letter aloud at the common table and Pipwort clapped, and my father had to look at his hands.
I opened the hive with mother and got stung on the wrist and did not cry, and she gave me the honey spoon.
Tamarisk and I found a path behind the berry rows that nobody else knows, and we keep it secret.

stances.why: Father says a clause you cannot read will catch you, and I want to read them all
Mother says it and the bees have proved it
It is mine and Tamarisk's and nobody else's
